gates.reason: Tests verify one captured auth identity is consistently used for cache keys, progressive requests, and monolith fallback, including Authorization headers.
Tests cover version skew, duplicate or late slices, cache races, fallback atomicity, rollback after partial failure, and preservation of last-good data.
Tests exercise progressive slice publication, worker decoding, avoidance of full-state fan-out, prompt fallback, and non-blocking cache reads.

Network requests use fixed same-origin API routes, encode slice keys, capture one auth token per load, and bind cache operations and fallback to that identity; no filesystem, command, SQL, LLM, or secret egress exists.

Slice keys are validated and deduplicated, every requested slice must arrive, version skew triggers atomic fallback, late results are suppressed, and cache/partial-state races are explicitly controlled.

Heavy slices fetch concurrently and decode in a worker when available, publish through a one-slice seam, avoid blocking on cache reads, terminate failed workers, and retain a bounded main-thread fallback.
Tests verify script-safe less-than escaping, absence of raw closing-script markup in the shell, exact application/json framing, and safe no-op behavior when rewrite anchors are absent.
Tests reproduce KPI field projection, defensive numeric coercion, deterministic grouping, envelope round-tripping, and correct replacement of skeleton values with real values.
Tests cover the parse-time shell surface and its in-place rewrite while keeping the generated shell fixed and dependency-free; no repeated request-time fan-out is introduced by the test code.

Dynamic HTML values are reduced to digits and commas, embedded JSON escapes every less-than character, and rewriting uses fixed literal boundaries rather than executable or attacker-controlled selectors.
KPI values come from explicit boot fields, are normalized to finite non-negative integers, are formatted deterministically, and the serialized envelope round-trips through JSON.
The dependency-free shell is constant-sized, generated with bounded string assembly, and runtime rewriting performs a small fixed number of linear string searches and splices per HTML response.
This test contains no auth, filesystem writes, network or LLM egress, DOM rendering, command execution, SQL, infrastructure configuration, or secret handling.
Tests reproduce lone-surrogate replacement in values and keys, preservation of valid pairs, strict-parser-safe output, standard JSON behavior, and nested dataset round-tripping.
This is bounded unit-test code and does not execute in an application hot path or ship a runtime surface.
The pure serializer performs no auth, filesystem, network or LLM egress, DOM insertion, command or SQL execution, infrastructure access, or secret handling.

The traversal replaces only unpaired UTF-16 surrogates, preserves valid pairs and toJSON behavior, handles keys and leaves, detects cycles, and retains JSON.stringify-compatible output for supported JSON-shaped data.
The implementation performs one linear scrub traversal before serialization, uses copy-on-change containers to avoid unconditional cloning, and maintains bounded recursion state with a WeakSet.
